plotHookRolled: hook.descent_into_darkness, hook.harvest_reckoning, hook.environmental_gauntlet
plotHookTaken:  hook.harvest_reckoning - the dyke guards the village's winter wheat; a failed mend leaves
the village a Blighted Harvest. The gauntlet survives as the crest, the descent as the culvert.
Seed dice: p3 mystery (compounded with the competing crew) - opposition time (the meltwater crest) -
agentRole competitor (brief override) - scale personal - system conditions.
--- The narrator's 12 questions, answered ---
1 P1 arrival?      Yes: {actor} arrives at {location} as the river rises with the thaw. Graph names.
2 P2 events?       A soft section of the dyke is seeping; the cost of a breach (the winter wheat) is stated.
3 P3 one stake?    Mystery (rolled): nobody knows why it is failing. Compounded on purpose with
{cast:ganger}'s cheaper crew piling sacks on it (competitor role).
4 <=80 words?      78 / 80 (opening + step-0 spine).
5 Read aloud?      Report throughout; no interior sensation.
6 Stated?          "Nobody knows why that section is failing." "If it breaks, the river will drown the winter wheat."
7 Every sentence works? Challenge, test or outcome.
8 Nothing unintroduced? Soft section, seep, sacks, crew and crest are in the step-0 spine; the culvert
is revealed by step 0's afterimages before step 1 names it.
9 One named person? {cast:ganger}; the reeve is a role noun.
10 Stake in a sentence? Can {actor} find why the dyke is failing and close it before the crest,
ahead of a cheaper crew?
11 Cards verb+noun? Remember The Old Craft, Raise Hidden Water, Ease Tired Backs, Hound A Rival,
Harden Wet Earth, Call A Hard Frost.
12 Opening per class? rural, written.
--- Mechanical design block ---
Crux            The village dyke is failing as the river rises, and nobody knows why.
Shape           Puzzle - Investigation - Resolution with the query-prize face. eye 0.56 (continue_weakened)
-> stone 0.64 (continue_weakened) -> stone 0.68 (fail_action). Linear, branch count 0.
Consequence hand (binding): story_seed (encounter_seed query #fellowship_errand on step 2 success) +
place (apply_condition trait.condition.location.harvest_blight on $here, step 2 failure). No swap.
Query prize     Step 2 rewardPool { possession: 1 } tagFilters [#ancient]: what the first builders left
under the culvert's old keystone.
Standing        reputation_with $here +0.06 / -0.06 on step 2; -0.02 on step 0 and step 1 failure (backs the
critical_failure chip on every route: a critical failure at any step ends the action).
Cost channels   All specials essence-priced. No Heavy Hand, no rider.
Cool failure    Nobody dies or is jailed. Failure is the village's harvest and the mason's name.
Accepted limit  No band-keyed step write: critical_failure writes Blighted Harvest (unchipped) only on its
step-2 route. The fellowship query can wither where no member accepts the subtype.
Proximity       encounter.town.levee_breach shares the harvest_blight place write on a flood premise.

stakes.goal: mend the failing dyke before the meltwater crest
stakes.risk: be blamed for breaking the dyke over the wheat
stakes.won: mended the dyke, and the lower fields stayed dry
stakes.lost: lost the race, and the river drowned the wheat

template.name: The Failing Dyke

openings.rural: {actor} arrives at {location} as the river rises with the thaw.

steps.narrativeTemplate:
The dyke that keeps the river off the lower fields has a soft section, and water is seeping through it. If it breaks, the river will drown the winter wheat.

Nobody knows why that section is failing. The reeve has sent for {actor} to find out and mend it before the meltwater crest. The reeve has also hired {cast:ganger}'s cheaper crew, who are piling sacks on top.
steps.criticalSuccessAfterimage: They found an old stone culvert under the soft section, its roof fallen in, and the ditch it drains into.
steps.successAfterimage: They found an old stone culvert under the dyke. Its roof has fallen in, and the river runs through the gap.
steps.successAtCostAfterimage: They found the collapsed culvert, but only after {cast:ganger}'s crew had piled sacks over the place to dig.
steps.failureAfterimage: They walked the dyke until dark and found only wet earth. They will have to dig blind.
steps.criticalFailureAfterimage: They read the seep wrong and told the reeve the dyke only needed height. The soft section burst at the first rise of water.

nudges.name: Remember The Old Craft
nudges.effectLine: Bring back a lesson they half forgot, so they know a long-dead builder's work when they find it.

bandProse.critical_success: {actor} remembered how old builders ran water under a bank, and walked straight to the culvert's mouth.
bandProse.success: {actor} remembered that old dykes often hide a drain, and went looking for one.
bandProse.near_miss: {actor} remembered the old trick late, after an afternoon on the wrong stretch.
bandProse.failure: {actor} remembered the old trick, and dug for a drain in the wrong place.

nudges.name: Raise Hidden Water
nudges.effectLine: Pull what seeps underground up to the surface, so the soft ground shows plainly where it runs.

bandProse.success: Water came up in a straight wet line across the dyke, right over the old culvert.
bandProse.success_at_cost: The wet line showed the culvert, and showed {cast:ganger}'s crew where to pile their sacks.
bandProse.failure: The ground darkened along the whole soft section, and showed them only what they already knew.
bandProse.critical_failure: Water came up all along the bank, and the whole dyke looked worse than it was.

steps.narrativeTemplate: The work now is to dig down through the soft section and make it sound before the crest. The sacks {cast:ganger}'s crew has piled are in the way of the dig. Wet earth slides back into the hole as fast as it is dug.
steps.criticalSuccessAfterimage: They dug down to the old culvert and had every fallen stone out of it by noon.
steps.successAfterimage: They dug down to the old culvert and cleared the fallen stone out of it.
steps.successAtCostAfterimage: They cleared the culvert, but had to pull down part of {cast:ganger}'s sack wall to do it.
steps.failureAfterimage: The hole kept filling with mud, and the culvert was only half cleared by dark.
steps.criticalFailureAfterimage: The sides of the hole slid in, and the river broke through the soft section.

critical_success.text: They know exactly where the culvert runs.

success.text: They found the culvert before they started digging.

success_at_cost.text: {cast:ganger}'s sacks are piled over the dig.

near_miss.text: They found the culvert late in the day.

failure.text: They are digging without knowing what is down there.

critical_failure.text: The reeve no longer trusts their reading.

nudges.name: Ease Tired Backs
nudges.effectLine: Wash the ache out of working bodies, so a crew keeps digging long after it should stop.

bandProse.critical_success: Nobody on the dig stopped to rest, and nobody needed to.
bandProse.success: The diggers worked through the afternoon without slowing.
bandProse.near_miss: The diggers kept going, but the light was failing before the last stone was out.
bandProse.failure: The diggers worked on without tiring, and the mud came in faster than they could lift it.

nudges.name: Hound A Rival
nudges.effectLine: Make an opponent's work go wrong in small ways, so they lose time they cannot spare.

bandProse.success: {cast:ganger}'s crew split three sacks and went back to the village for more.
bandProse.success_at_cost: {cast:ganger}'s crew lost their footing on the bank, and blamed {actor} for it in front of the reeve.
bandProse.failure: {cast:ganger}'s crew had every small trouble, and still kept piling sacks over the dig.
bandProse.critical_failure: {cast:ganger}'s crew slipped, and brought half their sack wall down into the hole.

steps.narrativeTemplate: The crest will come down the river tonight. {actor} must set a new roof on the culvert and close the dyke over it before the water arrives. {cast:ganger} tells the reeve the sacks will hold without it. By morning, the village will know whose work held.
steps.criticalSuccessAfterimage: The new culvert roof was set and covered by dusk, and the crest passed without a seep.
steps.successAfterimage: The dyke was closed over the new culvert before the crest, and it held through the night.
steps.successAtCostAfterimage: The dyke held, but the crest washed out {cast:ganger}'s sacks and flooded the nearest strip of wheat.
steps.failureAfterimage: The crest came before the dyke was closed, and the river went through onto the lower fields.
steps.criticalFailureAfterimage: The crest tore out the half-built culvert and a length of the dyke with it.

critical_success.text: The culvert is clear with half a day to spare.

success.text: The culvert is clear before dusk.

success_at_cost.text: {cast:ganger}'s crew is working against them now.

near_miss.text: The last of the culvert was cleared in the dark.

failure.text: The culvert is still half full of mud.

critical_failure.text: The soft section has already slumped.

effects.seedLabel: The Builders' Fellowship hears who mended the old culvert under the dyke, and has work for them.

nudges.name: Harden Wet Earth
nudges.effectLine: Make loose ground pack and set like old ground, so new work holds against water.

bandProse.critical_success: The new bank set hard by midnight, and the crest broke against it.
bandProse.success: The clay over the culvert set firm before the water reached it.
bandProse.near_miss: The clay set, but a seep opened at the foot of the bank and ran until dawn.
bandProse.failure: The clay set hard, and the water went round it through the old bank beside.
bandProse.critical_failure: The clay set like stone, and the crest tore the whole length out in one piece.

nudges.name: Call A Hard Frost
nudges.effectLine: Draw the warmth out of the air, so snow and ice melt slower and rivers rise later.

bandProse.success: A cold night up in the hills held the crest back until the work was done.
bandProse.success_at_cost: The crest came late, but it came higher than the reeve had ever seen.
bandProse.failure: Frost came back to the hills, and the crest came down on time anyway.

traitVariants.factorLine: Being Steadfast, they keep digging when the cold water comes in.
Being an Immovable Tyrant, they cannot get the village to dig for them.

template.description: A three-step expert Stone job in a village: the dyke that keeps a rising river off the lower fields is failing, and nobody knows why. The mortal finds the old stone culvert collapsed under it, digs down to clear it while a cheaper rival crew piles sacks on top, then sets a new culvert roof and closes the dyke before the meltwater crest. A held dyke pays an #ancient possession found under the culvert's old keystone, raises the mortal's standing with the village and plants a Builders' Fellowship sequel; a failed one leaves the village a Blighted Harvest and thinking less of the mortal.
